purpose: Rasburicase is used to lower high levels of uric acid in the blood, which can happen when certain cancer treatments break down tumor cells very quickly. This condition is called tumor lysis syndrome, and if uric acid builds up too much, it can seriously damage your kidneys. This medicine helps prevent or treat that problem.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes uric acid as a waste product when cells break down. Rasburicase is an enzyme — think of it like a tiny cleaning tool — that quickly converts uric acid into a harmless substance your body can flush out easily through your urine. This helps bring uric acid levels down much faster than other medicines.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, fever, headache, stomach pain, diarrhea, and rash are the most commonly reported side effects. Some patients may also feel tired or have low blood pressure during the infusion.
warnings: This medicine can cause a serious allergic reaction, including anaphylaxis, so you will be closely monitored while receiving it. It must NEVER be used in people with a condition called G6PD deficiency because it can cause life-threatening destruction of red blood cells (hemolytic anemia). It is also not safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Blood samples drawn from patients on this medicine must be handled in a special way — regular tubes can give false low uric acid readings.
typical_dosing: Rasburicase is given as an IV infusion (directly into a vein) once daily, usually over 30 minutes. The typical dose is 0.2 mg per kilogram of body weight, and treatment usually lasts about 5 days. Your cancer care team will decide the exact dose and length of treatment based on your specific situation.
